title: storage: mapped native-overlay whiteouts are omitted during image commit
body:
## Description

With native overlay storage and an explicit container UID/GID mapping,
`podman commit --squash=false` can return success while omitting deletion markers
from the resulting image layer. Files and directories removed from the container
then reappear in a container created from the committed image.

The failure originates in `storage/pkg/archive`: ownership mapping is attempted
before native overlay whiteouts are converted to archive whiteout entries.
Podman 6.1.1 provides the reproducer below.

## Steps to reproduce

Run this script as root on a disposable Linux host using Podman with native
overlay storage. It creates uniquely named containers and images and removes
those resources on exit. Save it as `reproduce.sh`, then run
`sudo bash reproduce.sh`. `PODMAN` can select a particular binary and `IMAGE` can
select a registry mirror of the same image digest.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [[ $(id -u) != 0 ]]; then
    printf 'Run on a disposable rootful Podman test host.\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

podman="${PODMAN:-podman}"
image="${IMAGE:-docker.io/library/alpine@sha256:7c8cb692ae09657cbc4a3f3cbd0e8d5a2690ba38386aaaf252dbb060bf5eb2e6}"
token="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/whiteout-repro.XXXXXXXX")"
name="$(basename "$token" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr . -)"
base_container="$name-base"
changed_container="$name-changed"
base_image="localhost/$name:base"
changed_image="localhost/$name:changed"
cleanup() {
    "$podman" rm --force "$base_container" "$changed_container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$podman" rmi "$changed_image" "$base_image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    rmdir "$token"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

"$podman" version
"$podman" run --name "$base_container" --network none \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$image" -ec \
    'mkdir -p /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; printf old > /whiteout-repro/remove-file; printf old > /whiteout-repro/remove-dir/file'
"$podman" commit --format oci "$base_container" "$base_image"

"$podman" run --name "$changed_container" --network none \
    --uidmap 0:1:65535 --gidmap 0:1:65535 \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$base_image" -ec \
    'rm /whiteout-repro/remove-file; rm -r /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-file; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-dir'

"$podman" diff "$changed_container"
"$podman" commit --format oci --squash=false "$changed_container" "$changed_image"

"$podman" run --rm --network none \
    --uidmap 0:1:65535 --gidmap 0:1:65535 \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$changed_image" -ec \
    'test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-file; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; printf "Deletion markers preserved\n"'
```

## Actual result

The deletion assertions succeed in the producer, and `podman diff` reports:

```text
C /whiteout-repro
D /whiteout-repro/remove-dir
D /whiteout-repro/remove-file
```

The subsequent commit exits **0**, but logs errors such as:

```text
Can't add file <upperdir>/whiteout-repro/remove-file to tar: host ID 0 cannot be mapped to a container ID; skipping
```

The deleted paths reappear in a container created from the committed image. The
script therefore fails its final absence assertions and exits **1**.

The same deletion loss occurs after saving the image and loading it into an
initially empty storage directory, so it is not limited to reuse in the original
store.

## Expected result

The committed layer contains the deletion whiteouts, and removed paths remain
absent in containers created from that image, including after save/load. The
script prints `Deletion markers preserved` and exits **0**.

## Environment and affected versions

| Component | Tested value |
|---|---|
| Podman | 6.1.1, commit `8303f2e25b675ea7f82099d615c60969aec15870` |
| Storage | `go.podman.io/storage` v1.64.0; tag `storage/v1.64.0`, commit `3aa788d1726dc0455117a1cc6290fffa14104f35` |
| Additional source regression | container-libs main commit `49fe7190f3ecd16fe4dcfd9e749ae480d4021a6c` |
| OS / architecture | Ubuntu 24.04, Linux amd64 |
| Kernel | 6.8.0-111-generic |
| Storage driver / backing filesystem | Native overlay / XFS |
| Podman execution | Rootful, inside an outer user namespace |
| Container UID and GID maps | `0:1:65535` |
| Go used for rebuilt binaries | 1.26.4 |

The test host provides an outer user namespace with 65,536 mapped UIDs/GIDs.
UID/GID values described below are relative to the namespace in which Podman
exports the layer.

The Alpine digest in the script was tested through a registry mirror; the direct
`docker.io` endpoint was not exercised in that environment.

## Root cause

The native overlay deletion entries were confirmed to be character devices
`0:0`, owned by UID/GID `0:0` in the exporting namespace.

In [`tarWriter.prepareAddFile`](https://github.com/containers/container-libs/blob/49fe7190f3ecd16fe4dcfd9e749ae480d4021a6c/storage/pkg/archive/archive.go),
`IDMappings.ToContainer` runs before `WhiteoutConverter.ConvertWrite`. The mapping
exemption checks for a `.wh.` filename, but the native deletion inode is still
named `remove-file` at that point. UID 0 is outside the container's mapping, so
ownership conversion fails. The archive walker logs the error and continues,
leaving the deletion out of the layer.

The [overlay whiteout converter](https://github.com/containers/container-libs/blob/49fe7190f3ecd16fe4dcfd9e749ae480d4021a6c/storage/pkg/archive/archive_linux.go)
would subsequently convert that inode into a `.wh.remove-file` archive entry.
That conversion needs to happen before deciding whether ordinary file ownership
mapping applies.

## Controls and candidate fix

A candidate patch converts whiteouts before ownership mapping, normalizes native
whiteout ownership to `0:0`, preserves explicit `ChownOpts` overrides, and copies
final directory ownership to synthetic opaque-directory markers. It applies to
both storage source commits above.

The following controls were run with otherwise equivalent original and patched
Podman 6.1.1 builds. Each case checks the committed image directly and after
save/load into an empty store:

| Case | Original | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Unmapped, unsquashed | Pass | Pass |
| Unmapped, squashed | Pass | Pass |
| Mapped, unsquashed | File, directory and nested-file deletions lost | Pass |
| Mapped, squashed | Pass | Pass |

The mapped unsquashed delta contains zero whiteouts before the patch and all
three expected whiteouts afterwards. Across the four cases, filesystem checks
improve from **42/48** to **48/48**. The minimal script above also fails before and
passes after the patch.

Seven whiteout regression cases fail against the original archive code and pass
against the candidate on both storage refs. Additional tests cover normal
file/directory ownership, opaque markers, ownership overrides and unmapped IDs.

Full archive-package runs on the candidate report **96 passed / 1 failed / 0
skipped** on main and **94 passed / 1 failed / 0 skipped** on v1.64.0. The failure
is the existing `TestTarWithBlockCharFifo`, which gets `EPERM` creating block
device `12:5` in the outer user namespace on both original and patched code. The
new character-device `0:0` whiteout tests execute successfully. `go vet`, gofumpt
and diff checks pass; the complete monorepo test/lint gate was not run.

The candidate addresses this whiteout conversion ordering bug; it leaves the
archive walker's broader log-and-continue error policy unchanged.
